A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffInk and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original handwriting-generation comparisons, model ablations, English generation examples, and an OCR augmentation experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, sampling-step experiments, style-mixing examples, and GLRNet augmentation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same InkVAE/InkDiT architecture, objectives, Algorithm 1, and default five-step DDIM procedure. The new style-mixing demonstration does not specify a modified component or generation algorithm.

E1.justification: CASIA-OLHWDB, IAM-OnDB, and ICDAR13 coverage is retained; English, one-shot, and paragraph generation already appear in v1. V2 Appendix C.1/Figure 11 adds a two-reference style-blending scenario, extending the evaluated input conditions and generation requirements.

E2.justification: V2 systematically adds Drawing (Zhang et al., 2017) and DeepImitator (Zhao et al., 2020) alongside WLU, SDT, and OLHWG in Table 1 and qualitative/layout comparisons. Appendix D.4 also adds real-only versus DiffInk-augmented GLRNet comparisons alongside CNN+Transformer, substantially expanding the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 changes the stated style-evaluator training data from the training set to the testing set, materially revising reported evaluation data use without establishing that results were rerun. V2 also introduces a 1–20-step DDIM sweep and a GLRNet OCR configuration. Generator splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained model ablations, v2 adds generated-versus-real feature-distribution analysis (Section 4.6/Figure 8), two-reference style-control cases (Appendix C.1/Figure 11), and DDIM quality–speed sensitivity analysis (Appendix C.4/Table 4). These substantially broaden analyses of realism, controllability, and sampling efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added scatterplots and sampling results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing rows in Tables 1–3 retain their scores, while v2 adds baseline, sampling, distribution, and style-mixing results. CNN+Transformer real-only/augmented CR/AR pairs change from 77.2/77.7 and 85.7/86.4 in v1 Table 4 to 83.9/84.2 and 89.6/90.0 in v2 Table 5, without explaining the replacement. New GLRNet pairs are 86.2/86.6 and 90.9/91.1. The new five-step sampling row reports DTW 1.052, versus the retained 1.049 in Tables 1–3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–9, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 rephrases the cross-entropy/CTC explanation without altering the losses; no theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning full-line latent diffusion, regularized InkVAE representations, conditional InkDiT generation, and superior quality and efficiency. Added experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of distributional overlap and DDIM sampling trade-offs, and reframes stitching errors around bounding-box prediction. It removes v1 Appendix D.2's explicit acknowledgment that requiring a reference for every target line is unrealistic. The multilingual retraining limitation remains.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is available and supplies a repository address. Appendix B.4 newly documents speed evaluation with batch size 1 on the same RTX A6000 GPU, excluding loading and preprocessing. These disclosures do not establish changes to the underlying timing runs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Tan et al. (2025) and Chen et al. (2025) to the latent-conditioning discussion, plus Zhao et al. (2020) and Peng et al. (2021) for added experiments. Drawing's Zhang et al. (2017) reference already existed. Section 2 and the central research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Local revisions affect experimental interpretation and appendix explanations; Appendix C reorders style consistency and comparisons, while existing one-shot/paragraph discussion moves from D.2 into D.5. Publication headers and several headings are updated.

P2.justification: V2 adds the distribution and style-mixing figures and a sampling-step table, expands Table 1 and the OCR table, and enlarges several visual comparisons with additional baselines. Retained illustrations are also relocated or resized, including the layout analysis and application examples. These substantially revise the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The DDIM sweep now supports the existing five-step efficiency choice, GLRNet broadens evidence for synthetic-data usefulness, and code/timing disclosures aid reproducibility. These provide a limited net benefit. Reporting weaknesses temper the gains: the evaluator-split and OCR-score revisions remain unexplained, and Table 5 implies gains of 5.7 CR and 5.8 AR points while its caption and prose retain the 8.5/8.6-point claims.
